summary.title: Deep Learning from First Principles
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a minimal deep learning engine in Rust using only the standard library, starting with a flat-buffer tensor type, Display formatting, and element-wise arithmetic.
keywords: how pytorch works under the hood
takeaways: Store tensors as a flat Vec<f32> plus a shape vector instead of Vec<Vec<f32>> to avoid pointer chasing and gain cache locality.
Map 2D indices to flat memory with row-major indexing: index = row * cols + col.
Validate tensor invariants (rank limited to 1D/2D, data length equals product of shape) with a custom error enum.
Implement element-wise add, sub, mul and div by sharing one helper that takes a closure, requiring identical shapes.
summary.summary: The guide walks through building a tensor library and neural network engine in Rust with no external crates. It explains tensor ranks, the mathematical notation for matrix elements, and why a flat Vec with a separate shape vector beats nested vectors. Each chapter follows a test-driven approach: write tests in a tests/ directory, implement the struct and methods, then verify with a small main program. The page covers Display formatting for matrices and element-wise operations so far, and says later chapters move on to linear regression and backpropagation.
